subject: Covariates on entry probabilities in jolly-seber super pop model

messages.author: f7b0e875c85b25ba
messages.subject: Covariates on entry probabilities in jolly-seber super pop model
parts:
Hey all, 

I was just curious if anyone has used covariates on the entry probabilities (b, or recruitment probs) in the Jolly-Seber super pop model outlined in chapter 10 in K&S. I am having some issues getting models to converge with realistic estimates, and I imagine my problem is that I am having trouble 'mimicking' the Dirichlet prior with a linear model.

Thanks in advance, 
-Dan

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: Covariates on entry probabilities in jolly-seber super pop model
parts:
Hi Dan,

AR is the sum of recruitable individuals (i.e., individuals in the augmented set that have never been alive). You could do something like this:

for(t in 2:T) {
  ER[t] <- exp(gamma0 + gamma1*x1[t] + ...) # Could include DD or make it per-capita
  AR[t] <- sum(recruitable[,t-1])
  b[t] <- ER[t] / AR[t] # Entrance probs
  }

for(i in 1:M) {
  for(t in 1:T) {
    recruitable[i,t] <- 1-max(z[i,1:t])
    }
   }


Note that ER must be less than AR, but as long as this condition is met with the initial values, it will hold. So initialize gamma0 to -20 or something.

Richard

OK, I think I had another typo. It should be:

​
recruitable[i,t] <- 1-max(z[i,1:(t-1)])

and so the for loop needs to be 2:T, not 1:T.

Once you have that part set up correctly, the model for the latent state (ignoring sites) would look something like:

z[i,t] ~ dbern(z[i,t-1]*phi + recruitable[i,t]*b[t])

Does that make sense? 

Richard

Hi everyone!

I have the same intention of modeling entry probs as a function of covariates.
I have tried to apply the Multinomial logit link function for the entry probabilities as suggested in chapter 10 of Kery&Shaub (2012) and as program MARK does.

    gamma ~ dnorm(0,0.0001) # Prior entry probs

    # Multinomial logit link for entry probabilities
    for(t in 2:n.visits){
      lgamma[t-1] <- exp(gamma)
      b[t] <- lgamma[t-1] / (1 + sum(lgamma[]))
    }
    b[1] <- 1 - sum(b[2:n.visits])

I am not sure how to proceed to the latent state (z[i,t]) . If I define:
for (i in 1:M){

for (t in 2:n.visits){
        # State process
        q[i,t-1] <- 1-z[i,t-1]
        mu2[i,t] <- phi[i,t-1] * z[i,t-1] + b[t] * prod(q[i,1:(t-1)])
        z[i,t] ~ dbern(mu2[i,t])
 
Is it correct? Or I need to restrict b[t] to conditional entry probs (nu[t]) as with the example with Dirichlet prior?
# Convert entry probs to conditional entry probs

nu[1] <- b[1]
    for (t in 2:n.visits){
    nu[t] <- b[t] / (1 - sum(b[1:(t-1)]))
    }#t

    mu2[i,t] <- phi[i,t-1] * z[i,t-1] + nu[t] * prod(q[i,1:(t-1)])


Any suggestion?
Em quarta-feira, 20 de abril de 2016 12:08:55 UTC-3, Richard Chandler escreveu:

OK, I think I had another typo. It should be:

​
recruitable[i,t] <- 1-max(z[i,1:(t-1)])

and so the for loop needs to be 2:T, not 1:T.

Once you have that part set up correctly, the model for the latent state (ignoring sites) would look something like:

z[i,t] ~ dbern(z[i,t-1]*phi + recruitable[i,t]*b[t])

Does that make sense? 

Richard

Hi Dan,

AR is the sum of recruitable individuals (i.e., individuals in the augmented set that have never been alive). You could do something like this:

​​
for(t in 2:T) {
  ER[t] <- exp(gamma0 + gamma1*x1[t] + ...) # Could include DD or make it per-capita
  AR[t] <- sum(recruitable[,t-1])
  b[t] <- ER[t] / AR[t] # Entrance probs
  }

for(i in 1:M) {
  for(t in 1:T) {
   
​​
recruitable[i,t] <- 1-max(z[i,1:t])
    }
   }


Note that ER must be less than AR, but as long as this condition is met with the initial values, it will hold. So initialize gamma0 to -20 or something.

Richard

Hi Dan,

I suggest developing the model in terms of the expected number of recruits, ER. Then derive the entrance probs as ER/AR where AR is the number of recruitable individuals. This approach allows for estimation of per-capita recruitment rates and density dependence.

Richard
